newsitem.title: USA: Spalding County, Ga., to hold consolidation vote.
newsitem.headline: Spalding County, Ga., to hold consolidation vote.

text.p: Georgia's Spalding County will vote on March 18 on a proposal to consolidate the City of Griffin and Spalding County governments, the Griffin Daily News reported.
Spalding County residents will also vote that day on a one-cent sales tax increase to fund school construction. Georgia voters approved a referendum in November giving school districts that option.

The tax increase would raise $41 million over five years. If it is rejected, the county will raise property tax rates by 11 percent in September to pay debt service on general obligation school bonds approved last fall.

The consolidation vote had originally been planned for last November, but was postponed because of federal rules requiring two 60-day notice periods for changes that could affect racial voting strength.
